land.text: the New South Wales territory south of the Murray River, 'the former Port Phillip District of NSW'

predecessors.note: Separated on 1 July 1851 (Territorial evolution of Australia; the colony page's infobox: 'Established: 1 July 1851').

land.text: Victoria, which 'federated with other colonies to form the Commonwealth of Australia' on 1 January 1901

successors.note: The State of Victoria is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier from 1 January 1901.

capitals.name: Melbourne
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Melbourne'; the page adds that 'Melbourne served as the temporary federal capital until the parliament moved to Canberra in 1927'.

correction.text: Victoria 'carved out of the southeastern part of the Colony of New South Wales', 'created from the former Port Phillip District of NSW'; the Territorial evolution page: 'created from the New South Wales territory south of the Murray River'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: modern Victoria (about 0.19 M km2 by the gazetteer) for 1851 to 1900. The Colony of Victoria page gives no area and no boundary, only the Murray River region as farmland; the Murray line is the Territorial evolution page's own wording. The colony kept the same extent to federation on the pages opened.

region.text: the New South Wales territory south of the Murray River, the former Port Phillip District

ledger.note: 1851: Victoria separates from New South Wales. 'Victoria was created from the New South Wales territory south of the Murray River' (1 July 1851); the colony page: 'independence from the Colony of New South Wales: 1 July 1851', 'Established: 1 July 1851'. The gold rush that began the same year ('The discovery of gold in 1851 near Ballarat and Bendigo') is not a border event.

1901: Victoria federates. The colony 'existed from 1851 until 1901, when it federated with other colonies to form the Commonwealth of Australia' on 1 January 1901 (infobox 'Federation of Australia: 1 January 1901').

wars.name: Eureka Rebellion
wars.outcome: 'The Eureka Rebellion of 1854, a miners' uprising against oppressive mining licenses and lack of representation'; no land changed hands and no rebel state held ground.
wars.note: The page gives the year, not the month or the outcome of the fighting.

certainty.note: The border with New South Wales is the Murray River, named in the Territorial evolution page; the western border with South Australia is the 141 E line of the 1836 letters patent (Territorial evolution page: South Australia lies 'between 132 degrees east and 141 degrees east'). Both are legal lines; no survey year is on the pages opened.

sources.title: Colony of Victoria

sources.title: Territorial evolution of Australia

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. 2 pages used: Territorial evolution of Australia (boundary, opened for the NSW dossier) and Colony of Victoria. The Eumerella Wars (from 1840, southwest Victoria; Australian frontier wars page) began under the Port Phillip District of New South Wales, before this colony existed, and are not listed here.
The Colony of Victoria page has no boundary, no area and no capital history. Cliopatria has no Victoria row; its British Colonial Empire row draws only settled land (see colony-of-new-south-wales notes). The 1850s gold-rush population, the Eureka stockade and the 1855 responsible government (23 November 1855) change no border and are not ledger events. Victoria as a state of the Commonwealth is carried by commonwealth-of-australia. The Murray River boundary is drawn with the modern Victoria admin-1 polygon, which differs from the river line by a few cells.
